outliers.summary: This video crushed because it weaponizes curiosity around an extreme, almost taboo question: what's the WORST job for your health? Will Tennyson's hook formula works on three levels. First, the title 'I Investigated The World's Unhealthiest Job' triggers immediate curiosity gap — viewers MUST know the answer. Second, the word 'Investigated' positions Will as a journalist/detective, not just another fitness creator, which broadens appeal beyond his core audience. Third, 'The boys are in Boise' in the description signals a buddy-trip vlog format, which keeps retention high because viewers stay for the personalities, not just the payoff. Will's channel average is 2.4M, but this hit 7.2M (2.9x) because the topic taps universal anxiety — almost everyone has worried 'is my job killing me?' That's a much wider net than typical fitness content like macro tracking or workout splits. The format combines investigative journalism + immersive vlog + shock value, which is highly shareable. People send this to coworkers, family, friends in that industry. Notice the sponsor stack too: MacroFactor, David Protein, Gymshark, cookbook — Will monetizes hard but the entertainment-first framing means viewers don't feel sold to. The lesson for creators: take a niche topic (health/fitness) and connect it to a universal human concern (your job, your environment, your daily life) using a curiosity-gap title and an investigative angle. The 'I tried/investigated/exposed' framing consistently outperforms 'here's what I learned' framing because it implies stakes and discovery.
